outcome: Maternal cardiac characteristics (left ventricular size, radial left ventricular function, longitudinal contractility, global longitudinal strain, cardiac index, left atrium size, left ventricular hypertrophy, filling pressures, E/e' ratio, maximal tricuspid regurgitation velocity, systolic pulmonary pressure)
cohort: The study included 65 pregnant women diagnosed with preeclampsia who underwent an echocardiographic examination during pregnancy.
finding: Changes in cardiac function in pregnant women with preeclampsia are observable across various echocardiographic parameters, and increased NT-proBNP levels are significantly associated with a decrease in gestational age at delivery.
cross-section timing: During pregnancy (when echocardiographic examinations were performed)
